title: Construct Binary Tree From String
description:
You need to construct a binary tree from a string consisting of parenthesis and integers.
The whole input represents a binary tree. It contains an integer followed by zero, one or two pairs of parenthesis. The integer represents the root's value and a pair of parenthesis contains a child binary tree with the same structure.
You always start to construct the left child node of the parent first if it exists.
 
Example 1:


Input: s = "4(2(3)(1))(6(5))"
Output: [4,2,6,3,1,5]

Example 2:

Input: s = "4(2(3)(1))(6(5)(7))"
Output: [4,2,6,3,1,5,7]

Example 3:

Input: s = "-4(2(3)(1))(6(5)(7))"
Output: [-4,2,6,3,1,5,7]

 
Constraints:

0 <= s.length <= 3 * 104
s consists of digits, '(', ')', and '-' only.
All numbers in the tree have value at most than 230.

def check(candidate):
    assert is_same_tree(candidate(s='4(2(3)(1))(6(5))'), tree_node([4, 2, 6, 3, 1, 5]))
    assert is_same_tree(candidate(s='4(2(3)(1))(6(5)(7))'), tree_node([4, 2, 6, 3, 1, 5, 7]))
    assert is_same_tree(candidate(s='-4(2(3)(1))(6(5)(7))'), tree_node([-4, 2, 6, 3, 1, 5, 7]))
    assert is_same_tree(candidate(s=''), tree_node([]))
    assert is_same_tree(candidate(s='1'), tree_node([1]))
    assert is_same_tree(candidate(s='1(2)'), tree_node([1, 2]))
    assert is_same_tree(candidate(s='1()(2)'), tree_node([1, 0, 2]))
    assert is_same_tree(candidate(s='10(20(30)(40))(50)'), tree_node([10, 20, 50, 30, 40]))
